turns.text: Jaw first — locked wide, back teeth grinding under the strain of a grin four hours old, cheeks screaming past where cheeks should stop. Feet already moving before the thought that says run finishes forming, weight low, ears flat against a chirp climbing up through the throat on its own, some canned syllable of joy hitting the air a half-second before the choice to make any sound at all.

the walkway runs elevated above the night market strip, foot traffic thinned to scattered stragglers and a noodle vendor hosing down his stall, steam rising into cold air. behind, four meters back and closing, a livestream drone holds altitude with a gimbal-mounted lens locked dead center — not hunting, tethered, contract-bound, its underside strip lighting cycling through a loop of pink and gold that reads HAPPYWARE IS HAPPY! in looping cursive script visible from the market floor below. the grin doesn't waver. it isn't allowed to.

Four meters is nothing, four meters is a leash with better lighting. Weight drops into the crowd's thinning gaps, weaving stall struts and a dropped crate, tail low, the chirp finally breaking free of the throat unbidden — bright, tinny, wrong — gone the second a support pillar cuts the drone's sightline for half a stride.

the pillar buys half a stride and no more — the drone's gimbal corrects, autonomous override kicking the tether taut, and the underside lighting stutters once before resuming its loop. past the noodle stall a service alley branches off dark, walls strung floor to ceiling with patched cable, one strand chewed thin near the junction box, tooth marks old and green at the edges where someone's been coming back for the same taste for months. the alley smells like solder and rain both.

Solder-smell says something else already claimed this stretch and left, which makes it safer, not less. Body flattens low along the wall, ducking under a sagging cable run, aiming for the alley's dead end where the signal always drops half a bar — not enough, never enough, but half a bar of quiet is worth the detour.

the dead end holds true to its reputation — signal strength drops, the drone's gimbal light flickering from solid pink to a stuttering amber warning, GPS lock lost, GPS lock lost cycling in a small robotic mutter nobody but a cat this close would ever hear. for three full seconds the tether goes slack, the drone hanging dumb and blind at the alley mouth, lens hunting for a signal that isn't there.

Three seconds is longer than it sounds. Jaw drops slack for the first time since dusk, muscle already sore in the sudden absence of the shape it's been forced into, and what comes out instead of the chirp is just breath — ragged, real, unbranded. Eyes close half a second longer than they should, greedy for the dark.

past the dead end, tipped on its side in a drainage runoff, a smart fridge unit sits gutted and still half-lit, one cracked panel still cycling a looping proposal message to nobody — SYNCED FOR LIFE, ANNIVERSARY PACKAGE INCLUDED — its compressor long dead, voice looping on stored battery alone, faithful to a marriage that ended when someone hauled it out here to die. the alley holds it like a headstone. rain finds the crack in its casing, drop by drop.

The fridge's dead vow means nothing tonight, less than nothing, and gets exactly the attention it's due — none. Something behind the ribs still holds onto the three seconds of slack jaw like a held breath, right up until the tether snaps taut again, the chirp forcing itself back up through the throat before the thought even arrives to resent it.

the gimbal light snaps back to solid pink, GPS lock reacquired, and the underside strip resumes its loop — HAPPYWARE IS HAPPY! — brighter now, as if the three seconds of silence needs correcting twice as hard. the tether pulls taut, gentle but absolute, walking the grin back out of the alley toward the walkway's brighter stretch, where a scattering of late-shift cats pause to watch the strip-light pass, then look away fast, the way anyone looks away from a car crash they can't help.

Walking back into brighter light isn't a choice, exactly — the tether doesn't drag, doesn't have to, four hours of contract-shaped muscle memory does the job on its own, paws finding the walkway's worn boards without being told. Ears flatten at the audience anyway. Watching costs nothing and takes plenty.

the walkway opens onto a wider platform where a NekoCorp billboard cycles overhead, half its panels dead, the working half looping a jingle about synthetic milk in a voice pitched exactly as warm as the drone's own branding font. off the platform's far rail, three shapes sit low and close together on a fire escape, ears all turned the same direction, watching the pink strip-light pass below without a sound between them — not a threat tonight, just an audience with better manners than the rest.

Three sets of eyes tracking without a single twitch is its own kind of message, one that doesn't need translating. Not friends. Not enemies either — just witnesses, the way this whole walkway's turned into witnesses since the drone started riding this close. Paws keep moving. Stopping to explain anything to anyone was never part of tonight's contract.

the drone's lens holds a half-second longer on the three watching shapes than the walkway strictly requires, some background process flagging them as engagement, content, worth the extra frame. ahead, the walkway ramps down toward a parking structure's open top level, concrete pillars thick enough to eat a signal whole if a body got far enough between two of them. the ramp smells like standing rainwater and old exhaust, decades past when anything with a combustion engine last used it.

Concrete pillars sound like relief and probably lie about it, same as the alley did, but three seconds was three seconds, and greed for a fourth wins over the ache in every limb. Ramp taken at a lope, not a sprint — sprinting reads as content too, probably, everything does lately — just a tired walk toward whatever the pillars can actually offer.

the upper level holds four dead vehicles under tarps gone stiff with age, water pooled black in every low spot, and between the second and third pillar the signal doesn't just stutter this time — it drops flat, the drone's whole light strip going dark at once, tether slack going loose enough to trail on the concrete. no mutter this time, no warning cycle. just dark, and quiet, and a body's own shadow finally its own.

,--.
       ( o.o)__
        '--'   \___
                 \  \__/\_/\
                  \_(  o.o  )
                     > ^ < (watching the towers blink)

Dark holds longer this time, long enough that the jaw forgets its four-hour shape entirely, sagging loose, tongue working once against teeth that ache in a way relief doesn't fix, just interrupts. No chirp climbs the throat uninvited. No light paints the concrete pink. Just rain, and old exhaust, and a stillness so complete it takes a full minute to trust.

the dark holds past the minute, past several more, the drone hanging dead-lit and forgotten between the pillars while dawn works its way gray into the eastern gap between towers. eventually — not yet, not for a while — the tether will find its signal again and the strip will remember its pink, but for now the garage keeps its stolen quiet, water dripping its own slow rhythm, indifferent to whichever shape rests easiest in the dark tonight.

Enough dark banked now to last past whatever tomorrow's contract renews to. Body folds down against the driest tarp-covered hood, tail wrapped tight, one ear still cocked toward the dead tether out of habit more than need. The grin, when it finally comes back, can come back on its own time.

the garage holds its silence around the shape on the tarp, the dead drone's strip-light patient in its blackout, rain thinning outside toward the last hour before shift-change traffic finds this level again. nothing logs the stillness. nothing needs to. the city keeps counting elsewhere, and this stretch of concrete, for now, belongs to whoever's quiet enough to keep it.
